title: Korea Ocean Business Corporation Act
full_text:
KOREA OCEAN BUSINESS CORPORATION ACT

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Act is to contribute to the development of the national economy by establishing the Korea Ocean Business Corporation to support shipping companies in acquiring vessels on a stable basis and securing liquidity, provide services necessary for the growth of the shipping industry, and thereby strengthen the competitiveness of the Republic of Korea's shipping industry.

Article 2 (Definitions)
The terms used in this Act are defined as follows: <Amended on October 24, 2023; September 16, 2025>
1. "Vessel" means a vessel under Article 2, subparagraph 1 of the Ship Safety Act;
2. "Shipping and port business" means any of the following businesses:
(a) Shipping business under Article 2, subparagraph 1 of the Marine Transportation Act;
(b) Port transport business under Article 2 (2) of the Port Transport Business Act and businesses prescribed by Presidential Decree among the port transport-related businesses under Article 2 (4) of that Act;
(c) Port development business under Article 2, subparagraph 7 of the Harbor Act and port hinterland complex development business under Article 2, subparagraph 12 of that Act (including such development projects implemented under other Acts);
(d) A business providing towage services at a trading port using tugboats under Article 2, subparagraph 4 of the Act on the Arrival and Departure of Ships;
(e) A business providing pilotage services under Article 2, subparagraph 1 of the Pilotage Act;
2-2. "Overseas port development business" means a business conducted outside the Republic of Korea in accordance with the laws of the country having jurisdiction, such as constructing, reconstructing, reinforcing, maintaining, repairing, operating, or dredging facilities designated as similar to port facilities, corresponding to port development business under Article 2, subparagraph 7 of the Harbor Act;
2-3. "Overseas port logistics business" means a business conducted outside the Republic of Korea under the laws of the country having jurisdiction that involves the development, reinforcement, maintenance, repair, or operation of shipping, port, or connected logistics facilities;
3. "Shipping and port business operator" means a person engaged in shipping and port business.

Article 3 (Legal personality)
The Korea Ocean Business Corporation (hereinafter referred to as the "Corporation") shall be a corporation.

Article 4 (Offices)
(1) The location of the Corporation's principal office shall be prescribed by its articles of incorporation.
(2) Where necessary to perform its affairs, the Corporation may establish branch offices or local offices as prescribed by its articles of incorporation.

Article 5 (Capital)
The capital of the Corporation shall be five trillion won and shall be contributed by the Government and other investors.

Article 6 (Shares)
(1) The capital of the Corporation shall be divided into shares.
(2) The shareholder rights pertaining to shares contributed to the Corporation by the Government shall be exercised by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries in consultation with the Minister of Finance and Economy. <Amended on October 1, 2025>
(3) Types of shares to be issued by the Corporation under paragraph (1), the amount per share, and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by its articles of incorporation.

Article 7 (Articles of incorporation)
(1) The articles of incorporation of the Corporation shall include the following:
1. Objectives;
2. Name;
3. Principal office, branches, and local offices;
4. Capital;
5. General meetings of shareholders;
6. Board of directors;
7. Officers and employees;
8. Affairs and their execution;
9. Accounting;
10. Method of public notice;
11. Issuance of bonds;
12. Amendments to the articles of incorporation;
13. Other matters prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) To establish or amend its articles of incorporation, the Corporation shall obtain authorization from the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 8 (Registration)
(1) The Corporation shall come into existence upon registration of its establishment at the location of its principal office.
(2) Matters concerning registration of its establishment under paragraph (1), registration of relocation and alterations, and other registration of the Corporation shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(3) The Corporation shall not assert against a third party any matter required to be registered until that matter has been registered. <Amended on February 18, 2020>

Article 9 (Relationship with other Acts)
Except as provided in this Act and the Act on the Management of Public Institutions, the provisions of the Commercial Act concerning stock companies shall apply mutatis mutandis to the Corporation.

Article 10 (Prohibition of use of similar names)
No person other than the Corporation established under this Act shall use the name "Korea Ocean Business Corporation" or any similar name.

CHAPTER II AFFAIRS AND ACCOUNTING

Article 11 (Affairs)
(1) The Corporation shall perform the following affairs: <Amended on December 8, 2020; October 24, 2023; March 31, 2026>
1. Investment in assets related to shipping and port business, such as vessels and port terminals;
2. Guarantees of debts incurred by shipping and port business operators to acquire assets related to shipping and port business, such as vessels and port terminals;
2-2. Guarantees of debts incurred by shipping and port business operators by providing assets related to shipping and port business, such as vessels and port terminals, as collateral;
2-3. Guarantees of debts incurred by shipping and port business operators from financial companies and other institutions defined in Article 2, subparagraph 3 of the Credit Guarantee Fund Act, where support for shipping and port business is necessary to respond to urgent economic or social crises or in other cases prescribed by Presidential Decree;
2-4. Bid guarantees and contract performance guarantees in relation to cargo transportation contracts concluded by shipping and port business operators;
3. Purchase and brokerage of bonds and shares related to shipping and port business;
4. Acquisition, management, and disposal of assets related to shipping and port business, such as vessels and port terminals, and the acceptance of entrustment of such activities;
5. Investment in and guarantees of debts related to overseas port development business and overseas port logistics business;
6. Duties of a specialized institution supporting the shipping industry under Article 40-2 (2) of the Marine Transportation Act;
7. Operation of the freight forward agreement market;
8. Training of specialized personnel in shipping, ports, and logistics;
9. Consulting on investments by shipping and port business operators in overseas logistics markets and related matters;
9-2. Support for enhancing the capacity of shipping and port business to respond to green management under Article 2, subparagraph 5 of the Act on the Promotion of the Transition to an Environment-Friendly Industrial Structure;
9-3. Support for enhancing the capacity of shipping and port business to respond to international environmental regulations imposed by international organizations, international agreements, and foreign governments;
10. Surveys and research relating to the affairs referred to in subparagraphs 1, 2, 2-2 through 2-4, 3 through 9, 9-2, and 9-3;
11. Affairs entrusted by the State, local governments, public institutions, or other entities;
12. Support for subsidies to shipping and port business operators as part of Government policy;
13. Other affairs prescribed by Presidential Decree to establish sound trading practices in shipping and port markets and promote industrial development.
(2) Following a resolution of its board of directors, the Corporation may make contributions or investments in corporations conducting any affairs specified in paragraph (1) or similar affairs.
(3) Matters necessary for performing the affairs under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 12 (Disposition of profits and losses)
(1) If net profits arise from the settlement of accounts for a fiscal year, the Corporation shall dispose of such profits in the following order:
1. Coverage of deficits carried forward;
2. Accumulation of at least 20 percent of net profits as an earned surplus reserve until the amount reaches the capital under Article 5;
3. Accumulation of at least 20 percent of net profits as a guarantee performance reserve until the amount reaches half of the capital under Article 5;
4. Distribution of dividends to shareholders as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) If a loss arises from the settlement of accounts for a fiscal year, the Corporation shall cover it from the reserve under paragraph (1) 3, then from the reserve under paragraph (1) 2 if the former is insufficient. The Government may cover any remaining amount.
(3) Reserves under paragraph (1) 2 and 3 may be transferred to capital as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 13 (Borrowing of funds)
Following a resolution of its board of directors, the Corporation may borrow funds or materials necessary for performing its affairs, including borrowings from foreign countries.

Article 14 (Issuance of bonds)
(1) The Corporation may issue bonds with approval from the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries to raise funds necessary for performing its affairs.
(2) The amount of bonds issued shall not exceed four times the sum of the Corporation's capital and reserves.
(3) The extinctive prescription of bonds shall be completed after five years for principal and two years for interest.
(4) Matters necessary for issuing bonds other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (3) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 15 (Guarantees of repayment)
The State may guarantee repayment of the principal of and interest on borrowings and bonds of the Corporation.

Article 15-2 (Maintenance of financial soundness)
The Corporation shall endeavor to maintain its financial soundness.

Article 16 (Subsidization of expenses)
Within their budgets, the State or local governments may subsidize or lend funds for expenses necessary for the non-profit-making projects that the Corporation performs under Article 11 (1) 12 and 13, or affairs entrusted under Article 11 (1) 11. <Amended on October 24, 2023>

Article 17 (Application of other Acts)
For purposes of applying Articles 64 through 67 of the Bank of Korea Act to the Corporation, the Corporation shall be deemed included among the financial institutions specified in those Articles.

Article 18 (Requests for provision of data)
(1) Where necessary for performing affairs under Article 11 (1), subparagraphs 1 through 4 and 11 through 13, the Corporation may request the State, local governments, shipping and port business operators, and other public organizations prescribed by Presidential Decree to provide necessary data. <Amended on October 24, 2023>
(2) Persons receiving requests under paragraph (1) shall comply unless there is a compelling reason not to do so. <Amended on February 18, 2020>
(3) When the purpose of data provided to perform its affairs has been achieved, the Corporation shall manage and delete that data in accordance with the Credit Information Use and Protection Act.

CHAPTER III SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

Article 19 (Supervision)
(1) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may supervise the Corporation in accordance with this Act and the Act on the Management of Public Institutions and issue orders necessary for such supervision.
(2) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may supervise the Corporation to ensure management soundness and issue necessary orders, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(3) Notwithstanding paragraph (2), the Financial Services Commission may conduct inspections necessary for maintaining the Corporation's management soundness as prescribed by Presidential Decree. In such cases, the Financial Services Commission shall notify the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries of the inspection results without delay.
(4) If the Financial Services Commission finds unlawful or improper acts by the Corporation as a result of an inspection under paragraph (3), it may request the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries to rectify such acts.

Article 20 (Submission of reports and inspection of documents)
(1) If the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries deems it necessary for supervision under Article 19, the Minister may require the Corporation to submit reports or direct public officials under the Minister's authority to inspect its business conditions, books, documents, or other necessary articles.
(2) If the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries deems it necessary, the Minister may entrust inspections under paragraph (1) to the Governor of the Financial Supervisory Service.
(3) The Minister of Finance and Economy or the Financial Services Commission may request the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries to require submission of reports or inspection of documents under paragraph (1) when deemed necessary. <Amended on October 1, 2025>
(4) Persons conducting inspections under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall carry identification indicating their authority and present it to the persons concerned. <Amended on February 18, 2020>

Article 21 (Appointment of agents)
The president of the Corporation may appoint an agent from among its officers and employees who is authorized to perform all judicial or extrajudicial acts concerning its affairs, as prescribed by the articles of incorporation.

Article 22 (Duty to maintain confidentiality)
No current or former officer or employee of the Corporation shall disclose secrets learned in the course of performing their duties.

Article 23 (Penalties)
A person who discloses secrets learned in the course of performing official duties in violation of Article 22 shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than two years or by a fine not exceeding 20 million won.

Article 24 (Administrative fines)
(1) A person who uses the name "Korea Ocean Business Corporation" or a similar name in violation of Article 10 shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding five million won.
(2) Administrative fines under paragraph (1) shall be imposed and collected by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

ADDENDA <Act No. 15359, January 16, 2018>

Article 1 (Enforcement date)
This Act shall enter into force on July 1, 2018.

Article 2 (Preparations for establishment of the Corporation)
(1) Before this Act enters into force, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall establish the Committee for Establishment of the Korea Ocean Business Corporation (hereinafter referred to as the "Establishment Committee") to handle affairs concerning the establishment of the Corporation, including determination of the time of its establishment.
(2) The Establishment Committee shall consist of not more than seven establishment committee members, including one chairperson.
(3) Establishment committee members shall be commissioned by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries, and the Vice Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall serve as chairperson of the Establishment Committee.
(4) The Establishment Committee shall prepare the articles of incorporation of the Corporation and obtain authorization from the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries.
(5) The Establishment Committee shall be deemed the executive recommendation committee under Article 29 of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions until the initial board of directors is formed.
(6) Upon obtaining authorization under paragraph (4), the Establishment Committee shall register the establishment of the Corporation.
(7) Upon completing registration of establishment under paragraph (6), the Establishment Committee shall transfer its affairs and property to the president of the Corporation.
(8) The Establishment Committee shall be deemed dissolved upon completion of the transfer of affairs and property under paragraph (7).

Article 3 (Expenses of establishment)
Expenses incurred in establishing the Corporation shall be borne by the Corporation.

Article 4 (Succession to property, rights and obligations)
(1) Upon the establishment of the Corporation, it shall comprehensively succeed to the property, rights, and obligations of Korea Maritime Guarantee Insurance Co., Ltd. and Korea Ship and Ocean Co., Ltd. In such cases, the Corporation shall be deemed licensed under Article 4 of the Insurance Business Act, limited to the business of maintaining insurance contracts concluded by Korea Maritime Guarantee Insurance Co., Ltd. before this Act enters into force; the Insurance Business Act shall not apply to the insurance contracts concerned.
(2) Upon establishment of the Corporation, it shall comprehensively succeed to the property, rights, and obligations of the specialized institution supporting the shipping industry designated under Article 40-2 (1) of the Marine Transportation Act.
(3) Upon establishment of the Corporation, the names of the respective companies and institutions recorded in registries and other official books concerning the property, rights, and obligations comprehensively succeeded to under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be deemed the name of the Corporation.
(4) The value of property succeeded to by the Corporation under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be its appraised value at the time of succession.

ADDENDA <Act No. 16703, December 3, 2019>
This Act shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

ADDENDA <Act No. 17054, February 18, 2020>
This Act shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

ADDENDA <Act No. 17619, December 8, 2020>
This Act shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation: Provided, That the amended provisions of Article 11 (1) 2-3 shall enter into force six months after the date of promulgation.

ADDENDA <Act No. 19777, October 24, 2023>
This Act shall enter into force three months after the date of its promulgation.

ADDENDA <Act No. 21059, September 16, 2025>
This Act shall enter into force six months after the date of its promulgation.

ADDENDA (Government Organization Act) <Act No. 21065, October 1, 2025>

Article 1 (Enforcement date)
This Act shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation: Provided, That the parts amending Acts under Article 7 of these Addenda which were promulgated before this Act enters into force but have not yet entered into force shall enter into force on the respective dates on which those Acts enter into force, and the following amended provisions shall enter into force on the dates specified in the relevant subparagraphs:

1. The following amended provisions shall enter into force on January 2, 2026: Provided, That parts of Acts amended under Article 7 of these Addenda (limited to those relating to items (a) and (b)) which were promulgated before the date specified in the main sentence of this subparagraph but have not yet entered into force shall enter into force on the respective dates of those Acts:
(a) Amended provisions of Article 19 (4), Article 23, Article 29 (1) 1, and Article 30;
(b) Amended provisions of Article 12 (2), Article 19 (3), Article 22, and the proviso of Article 29 (2) (limited to provisions concerning the Minister of Finance and Economy and the Ministry of Finance and Economy);
(c) Acts amended under Article 7 of these Addenda (limited to those relating to the amended provisions of items (a) and (b)).
2. Omitted.

Articles 2 through 6 Omitted.

Article 7 (Amendments to other Acts)
(1) through (518) Omitted.

(519) Part of the Korea Ocean Business Corporation Act shall be amended as follows:

In Articles 6 (2) and 20 (3), "Minister of Economy and Finance" shall in each case be replaced with "Minister of Finance and Economy".

(520) through (626) Omitted.

Article 8 Omitted.

ADDENDA <Act No. 21518, March 31, 2026>
This Act shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.
